name: Particle-1
archDisplay: Rank-64 LoRA adapter (about 1.25% of the base parameter count) on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, a 552B sparse MoE causal encoder-decoder (~8B active in prefill, 16B in decode)
note: First model from Particle, the San Francisco startup Suhail (Mixpanel's founder) announced on Oct 28, 2026. It is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash post-trained with GSPO reinforcement learning (a rank-64 LoRA on the experts) to finish software-engineering tasks with fewer tokens: Particle reports 28.4-52.2% fewer output tokens and 34.4-51.6% lower cost per task than the base on Terminal-Bench 2.1, ReactBench, ADE Bench and DeepSWE 1.1, with pass@1 inside the base model's confidence intervals. Weights are not released; it is served through the Particle API (and Vercel AI Gateway). Price is the Particle docs' $0.25/$1.00 per Mtok (cached input $0.03); the launch post's cost footnote assumes $0.30/$1.20. paramsB/activeParamsB are the base model's, since the adapter does not change the served architecture. NOT FILED: per-benchmark coding pass rates (the post shows them in an unlabelled chart toggle); Tau Airlines 86.00 (the post does not say which tau-bench version); BabyVision with tools 89.18 has no corpus column.
